biodiversity_overview.text: 396 GBIF occurrence records for 14 tracked species are attributed to Mizoram, spanning 1951-2026.
372 of these records (93.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 8, Magnoliopsida 4, Actinopterygii 1, Mammalia 1.

threatened_species.text: 1 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Cuckoo (136), Indian White-eye (134), Mango (68), Indian Gooseberry (17), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (14).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1 in 2016 to 48 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.76% of Mizoram's area (9 areas intersect the state).
11.8% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (44 of 372); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Indian Glass Perch (0.19), Mango (0.18), Indian Nuthatch (0.15), Indian Trumpet Tree (0.13).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Mizoram (equal-weight reference): cell near 22.125N 92.625E (overall rank 313, median rank across weightings 314); cell near 22.875N 92.625E (overall rank 352, median rank across weightings 340); cell near 23.625N 92.625E (overall rank 376, median rank across weightings 374).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 21,036 km2 (91.24% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

3,741.9 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (17.79% of the 2000 extent; 13.64% in 2015-2024, rank 2 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2017 (459.52 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.13% of land and population density is 59.8 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
9% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
